claim: For the realistic qubit-teleportation protocol of Trump, Bruß, and Lewenstein in which Alice sends the maximum-posterior Bell label inferred from photon-number detection after one polarization-preserving beamsplitter, with an ideal maximally entangled resource and a Haar-uniform unknown pure qubit, the exact maximal average teleportation fidelity is \(\bar F_{\max}=5/6\), attained by the standard 50:50 analyzer. The two Bell states \(\lvert\phi^+\rangle\) and \(\lvert\phi^-\rangle\) induce identical photon-count distributions for every such beamsplitter, so the maximum-a-posteriori Bell-label success probability is at most \(3/4\); a 50:50 analyzer attains this by perfectly distinguishing \(\lvert\psi^+\rangle\) and \(\lvert\psi^-\rangle\) and guessing within the unresolved \(\phi\)-pair. A correct Bell label gives fidelity one, while any wrong Pauli correction has Haar-average pure-state fidelity \(1/3\), hence \(\bar F=(1+2p_{\mathrm{MAP}})/3\le 5/6\). Therefore the source's reported numerical maximum \(\bar F_{\max}\approx0.88\) is not the Haar-uniform average over pure input states; the corrected value remains above the classical \(2/3\) benchmark and does not challenge the source's qualitative conclusion that incomplete linear-optical Bell analysis can still demonstrate nonclassical teleportation.

integrity.proof_dependence: The ceiling and attainability are analytic. The checker replays exact rational consequences and is not used as an infinite proof.
integrity.source_date_evidence: arXiv:quant-ph/0010113v1 records first public submission on 2000-10-31.

scientific_limitations: The claim uses normalized Haar measure on pure qubit inputs and is restricted to the source's single polarization-preserving beamsplitter with ideal photon-number-resolving detection and maximum-posterior Bell-label correction.

The source does not provide its numerical integration code; the calculation proves the Haar value \(5/6\) but does not identify the exact coordinate weighting responsible for the printed \(\approx0.88\).
Ancillary photons, active optics, adaptive networks, nonlinear interactions, or other Bell analyzers are outside the bound.
title: A sharp \(5/6\) Haar-fidelity ceiling for single-beamsplitter realistic teleportation
